sharpedge_projection.reason: Model-market separation was only 1.5 points toward the Under, below the LIVE-FLOW strike threshold for an end-of-third-quarter market.

checkpoint_diagnostics.key_read: Phoenix's 33-point third quarter was powered by extreme shooting efficiency and created a reasonable regression case, but the sportsbook had already moved to 186.5. SharpEdge's frozen 185.0 fair produced only a 1.5-point Under gap, which was insufficient for a strike given fourth-quarter foul and efficiency volatility.

what_we_got_right: SharpEdge froze a 185.0 market-blind fair total before sportsbook comparison.
William Hill posted 186.5, leaving only 1.5 points of theoretical Under edge, and SharpEdge correctly refused to force the wager.
Phoenix's third-quarter shooting spike was recognized as regression-prone without assuming that team regression automatically meant full-game Under value.
The no-bet decision avoided a losing Under; the game finished 188.
Fourth-quarter volatility was correctly respected at the decision stage.
important_game_mechanics: Phoenix did regress from 33 Q3 points to 21 Q4 points, but Atlanta scored 26 in the fourth quarter and prevented total-game regression from materializing enough.
Atlanta shot 53.3% in Q4 and Phoenix shot 54.5%.
The teams combined for 19 fourth-quarter free-throw attempts and made 16, keeping the scoring floor elevated.
Angel Reese scored 13 points in the fourth quarter on 5-for-5 shooting and finished with a career-high 31 points.
Atlanta committed only one fourth-quarter turnover, preserving offensive efficiency and possession quality.
risk_notes: A 1.5-point theoretical edge at -115 is too thin to absorb fourth-quarter variance.
Late-game foul rates can erase modest Under edges quickly, particularly in competitive games with star offensive concentration.
Do not equate regression in one team's scoring with sufficient regression in the full-game total.

model_reinforcement.name: LIVEFLOW_END3Q_EDGE_THRESHOLD_v1
rules: At end-of-third-quarter checkpoints, require a larger model-market gap than 1-2 points before attacking a total.
Continue freezing market-blind projection before sportsbook comparison.
Separate team-level regression from full-game regression; the opposing offense can offset the decline.
Explicitly account for late free-throw and foul volatility as upside tail risk to live Unders.
Log disciplined passes with the same audit detail as wagers so no-bet decisions become training data.

postmortem.lesson: This checkpoint validates the pass discipline. SharpEdge had 185.0 against 186.5, only a 1.5-point Under gap. Phoenix did cool in Q4, but Atlanta stayed efficient and the teams combined for 47 points, producing a 188 final. The important result is that insufficient edge was not converted into unnecessary bankroll exposure.
